cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Paper 2 of OCR J271 GCSE Law covers Law in Action — it is worth 80 marks and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Paper 2 Section A covers the Law of Tort: negligence, occupiers' liability, nuisance and remedies

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Paper 2 Section B covers two options from: Law of Contract, Consumer Protection, Company Law, Employment Law, Intellectual Property and Data Protection

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Alternatively, Section B may cover Rights and Responsibilities and Criminal Law in Context depending on the school's chosen options

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Paper 2 contains the same mix of question types as Paper 1: short-answer (1-4 marks), medium-answer (5-10 marks) and extended-response (15 marks)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: The same timing principle applies: 90 minutes for 80 marks, roughly 1 minute per mark

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: For tort scenario questions in Section A, use the ILAC method: identify the tort, state each element (duty of care, breach, damage for negligence), apply to the facts and conclude on liability

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: For negligence questions, always work through the three elements in order: duty of care (Caparo test), breach (reasonable person standard), and damage (causation and remoteness)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: For Section B, ensure you have revised the specific optional topics your school has chosen — do not prepare topics that will not appear on your paper

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Evaluation questions in Paper 2 often ask you to assess the effectiveness of a legal rule or the fairness of a legal principle — use the same balanced approach as Paper 1

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Scenario questions in tort law require careful factual analysis — each element of the tort must be connected to specific facts from the scenario

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper 2: Law in Action Technique
cards.back: Always use case authority to support your analysis — for negligence, key cases include Donoghue v Stevenson, Caparo v Dickman, Bolitho v City and Hackney HA and Page v Smith

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — paper 2: law in action technique?
cards.back: 1. For Paper 2: Law in Action Technique questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Paper 2: Law in Action Technique 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant

AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of paper 2: law in action technique to legal scenarios and problems, using legal reasoning and analysis. AO3 (Analysis & Evaluation): Analyse, evaluate and critique
